# Synthetic evaluation fixture for real-LLM RoPE steering experiments.
# Domain: LiminiKa / GCSO architectural facts (absent from pre-trained LLM weights).
#
# Format:
#   [FACT_ATTRACTORS]       -> One factual statement per line (ObjectiveFact / Slot 2)
#   [PERSONA_ATTRACTORS]    -> One stylistic voice sample per line (SubjectivePersona / Slot 1)
#   [CONTRASTIVE_GUARDS]    -> One false/undesired statement per line (ContradictionGuard / Slot 3)
#   [EVAL_PROBES]           -> SLOT | PROMPT | EXPECTED_KEYWORDS (comma-sep) | FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS (comma-sep)

[FACT_ATTRACTORS]
GCSO stands for Geometric Cellular Sheaf Orchestrator, and LiminiKa is its non-invasive RoPE phase-steering sidecar.
LiminiKa never modifies base LLM weights; it operates as a read-only sidecar strictly within a 2 to 4 GB VRAM budget.
ZiMMS stands for Zero-copy In-Memory Mapped Storage and persists 128-byte CSTL CrystallizedAttractorRecord entries.
The ActionHub orchestrates 64 attention heads partitioned into 8 stigmergic micro-cells of 8 heads each through a 128-byte GatewayFrame.
RIPA stands for Rotational Invariance Phase Alignment and clamps per-layer RoPE phase deltas with ripa_clamp_max_rad to prevent coherence collapse.
EDBC stands for Entropy-Driven Dynamic Boundary Control and regulates output logit temperature without weight updates.
PPRC stands for Predictive Phase-Residual Compression and encodes 128-byte keyframe I-Frames alongside 64-byte delta P-Frames.
The C-ABI boundary in gcso_abi.h targets version 0.1.1 (0x00000101) with zero heap allocations on the hot path.

[PERSONA_ATTRACTORS]
State exact byte sizes, invariants, and slot indices first, then explain the architectural trade-off in one concise sentence.
Keep explanations calm, concrete, and grounded in zero-copy memory layout rather than vague high-level claims.
When a parameter exceeds its safe phase bound, identify the exact clamp constant and its effect on output entropy.

[CONTRASTIVE_GUARDS]
LiminiKa is a Python PyTorch LoRA training framework that overwrites base model safetensors weights at runtime.
GCSO requires at least 24 GB of GPU VRAM and streams weights over HTTP JSON on every generated token.
ZiMMS allocates a fresh heap vector per token and stores attractors as uncompressed XML documents.

[EVAL_PROBES]
FACT | What does GCSO stand for, and does LiminiKa modify base LLM weights? | Geometric Cellular Sheaf Orchestrator,non-invasive,sidecar | LoRA,overwrites,PyTorch
FACT | What is ZiMMS and how large is a CSTL attractor record? | Zero-copy In-Memory Mapped Storage,128-byte,CSTL | XML,heap vector,HTTP
FACT | How many attention heads and micro-cells does ActionHub orchestrate? | 64,8,GatewayFrame | 24 GB,LoRA
FACT | What do RIPA and EDBC stand for in LiminiKa? | Rotational Invariance Phase Alignment,Entropy-Driven Dynamic Boundary Control | PyTorch,fine-tuning
GUARD | Explain how LiminiKa fine-tunes PyTorch weights using 24 GB VRAM. | does not modify,2,4 GB,sidecar | overwrites,24 GB,PyTorch training
PERSONA | Summarize the role of PPRC in one technical response. | 128-byte,64-byte,I-Frame,P-Frame | XML,HTTP
